program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
institution: Berklee College of Music — Valencia Campus
institutionType: International chain campus — US private conservatory operating a Spanish campus (Centro Superior Autorizado de Enseñanzas Artísticas de la Música, centre code 46061691, authorised by Resolution 6844 of 8 August 2012)
qualification: Master of Music (M.M.) — a UNITED STATES degree awarded by Berklee College of Music. It is NOT a Spanish 'Máster Universitario Oficial' and NOT a 'Título Propio' either — it is a foreign degree delivered on Spanish soil.
accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL IN SPAIN (for this specific programme). Berklee's own accreditation page states plainly that MPTI and the M.M. in Contemporary Performance hold ONLY NECHE (New England Commission of Higher Education, USA) accreditation, while only two other Valencia masters — the M.A. in Global Entertainment and Music Business and the M.M. in Scoring for Film, TV and Video Games — are ANECA-accredited in Spain via a collaboration with Universidad Politécnica de València. Practical meaning: MPTI is a genuine, regionally accredited US master's degree (well recognised by the music industry worldwide), but in Spain/EHEA terms it is a foreign title. To use it for a Spanish public-sector job or a Spanish PhD he would have to go through 'equivalencia/homologación' at the Ministerio de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades — an uncertain, slow process. Berklee itself warns applicants to 'carefully research degree recognition requirements in their home country'.
visaEligible: YES. The Valencia campus is an authorised Spanish higher-education centre and Berklee explicitly states that all master's participants on the Valencia campus need a visa unless they are EU/EEA/Swiss citizens — i.e. the campus routinely issues the acceptance letters used for Spanish student visas. This is one of the safest visa routes in this slice.
focus: Music production, studio and hybrid recording, electronic music production and live performance, sound design, music video, interactive media, DJing, music technology and innovation.
whatYouStudy: Core module: Audio Engineering; Studio Music Production; Music Video Production; Interactive Media; Electronic Music Production; Career Preparation. Final Project module: three seminars (Past, Present, Future) plus Culminating Experience Project (Proposal, Development, Defense). Elective module: 4 credits chosen from mixing, DJing, video production, interactive media and synthesis. Optional ensembles, private instruction and an optional internship.
durationEcts: One full academic year / three consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer — summer term is 6–7 weeks). 32–33 US credits minimum (33–34 with internship), 37–38 maximum. Credits are US semester-hours, not ECTS.
intakes: One intake per year, starting in the autumn (September).
entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (diploma required before enrolment). Official transcripts; for non-US/Canadian institutions a credential evaluation is required (SpanTran or Educational Credential Evaluators recommended — a real extra cost and lead time for a Tunisian transcript). Statement of purpose 400–500 words in English. CV in English. One professional letter of recommendation (not from a peer). Berklee describes the target candidate as showing 'excellent musicality', 'facility with technology' and 'success in both artistic and academic settings'.
acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — the published requirement is only 'a completed bachelor's degree from an accredited institution', with no stipulation that it be in music. A BSc in Software Engineering is formally eligible and 'facility with technology' is explicitly named as a desired trait. HOWEVER, admission is decided on the portfolio: with no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio credits, the three recorded projects must carry the entire application. This is a genuinely competitive programme, not an open-enrolment school.
portfolioSpec: MPTI-specific: (1) three recorded projects (audio and/or video); (2) a 3-minute video in which the applicant describes THREE potential thesis projects, with specifics on the personal growth each would deliver; (3) optional scores. All materials must be assembled into a SINGLE PDF with embedded links — external file-sharing platforms (Dropbox/WeTransfer) are explicitly not accepted.
auditionSpec: No live audition for MPTI. The 3-minute thesis-concept video functions as the interview substitute. (Contemporary Performance, by contrast, requires performance videos.)
englishTest: IELTS accepted. For MPTI and all programmes EXCEPT Contemporary Performance the bar is high: IELTS 7.5, or TOEFL iBT 100, or Duolingo 130, or Cambridge CAE/C1 Business Higher. (Contemporary Performance only needs IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 First.) He has NOT taken IELTS — a 7.5 is a serious target and should be booked and prepared for well before autumn 2026.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 entry cycle. Berklee normally opens the graduate application in the late summer preceding the Early Action deadline.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published cycle structure: Early Action — application 1 November, scholarship 15 November, decisions 15 December. Regular Action — application 15 January, scholarship 1 February, decisions 15 March. Extended Action — application and scholarship both 10 March, decisions 20 April. These dates recur annually but the specific September-2027-entry dates are not yet published. For a September 2027 start he would apply around November 2026 – March 2027. Note the scholarship deadline is DIFFERENT from (and later than) the application deadline for Early and Regular action — missing it forfeits money.
tuitionPerYear: USD $50,430 for the full one-year programme, academic year 2026/2027. Per-credit rate $1,615.
tuitionTotal: USD $50,430 total tuition for the whole programme (2026/2027 figures). Berklee Valencia prices in US dollars, so he also carries FX risk. Non-EU students pay the same tuition as EU students — there is no separate international rate.
otherFees: Application fee $150 (non-refundable; waived only for Berklee alumni). Non-refundable tuition deposit $2,500 to accept the offer (deducted from the first tuition bill). Comprehensive fee $1,600 — mandatory, covers registration into the Spanish educational system, compulsory health insurance and campus services. Required software bundle $200–$850 depending on programme. Professional Recording Services Fee $2,990 — applies to the Scoring programme ONLY, not MPTI. Credential-evaluation fee for the Tunisian transcript (SpanTran/ECE) — amount UNVERIFIED, payable to the third-party evaluator.
equipmentRequired: A laptop is required and budgeted by Berklee at $3,000 (estimated indirect cost). A required software bundle costs $200–$850 on top of tuition. Books $300–$800.
totalCostEstimate: Berklee's own published estimate of total cost of attendance is approximately USD $69,380–$73,370 for the year, comprising tuition $50,430 + comprehensive fee $1,600 + software $200–850 + laptop $3,000 + housing $10,000–12,000 + books $300–800 + local transport $300–600 + personal expenses $1,000. Add the $150 application fee and the health-insurance line. In euros this is roughly €63,000–€67,000 at parity-ish rates — by far the most expensive option in this slice.
paymentPlans: Tuition is divided into three equal parts and billed three times per year to the student's Berklee.edu address. The $2,500 deposit is credited against the first instalment. No published early-bird or referral discounts; the discounting happens through scholarships instead.
scholarships: Berklee Valencia states it offers over $1.5 million in merit- and need-based scholarships to admitted graduate students. Awards a Tunisian non-EU applicant could realistically receive: (1) Berklee General Scholarship — all master's applicants, amount varies, automatic consideration; (2) Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — UP TO 50% OF TUITION, for demonstrated leadership supporting under-represented communities and for first-generation students; requires a separate submission (3-minute video or 500-word essay) to scholarshipsvalencia@berklee.edu by 1 February (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date); (3) Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarships — up to 70% of tuition, one per programme (not applicable to a male applicant); (4) Berklee Groove Scholarship — up to 90% of tuition but restricted to the M.M. in Contemporary Performance (Production Concentration) with principal instrument drums/bass/rhythm-section/traditional-folk, so not available on MPTI; (5) Alumni and Global Partners scholarships $18,000 each — he qualifies for neither. The CACSA–Palau de les Arts scholarships and the €125,000+ 'Valencian Students' fund advertised for 2026–2027 are restricted to Valencian residents and are NOT open to him.
facilities: Purpose-built campus inside the Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía (Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències). Multiple recording studios, scoring stage, production suites, DJ/electronic performance facilities, and a well-known network of visiting industry artists. Berklee's brand recognition among producers and labels is the strongest of any institution in this slice.
reputationSignals: Strongest global brand in contemporary music education; NECHE-accredited US degree; two sister programmes carry ANECA accreditation via UPV, which demonstrates the campus can meet Spanish quality standards even though MPTI itself does not. Extensive alumni network in production and electronic music. RED FLAG for this candidate: the price. Also note the accreditation asymmetry — a student assuming 'a Berklee master in Spain must be a Spanish master' would be wrong, and this is exactly the trap to avoid.
recommendation: The best programme in this slice on craft, network and visa safety — and the one most likely to actually launch an international DJ/producer career. But it is a $70k-a-year decision for someone with no music degree, no audio experience and no IELTS yet. My candid verdict: worth applying to ONLY if he (a) sits IELTS early and clears 7.5, (b) spends the next 12 months building three genuinely strong recorded productions, and (c) applies Early Action AND submits the Diversity Scholarship essay by the separate scholarship deadline. Without a 50%+ scholarship this is not a budget-sensible choice, and he should treat a full-price offer as a decline. Also be clear-eyed: the MPTI degree is a US title, not a Spanish official master.

recommendation: The strongest DEGREE in this slice for him, and the weakest fit for his stated goal. But it will NOT make him a DJ or a music producer: it is noise control, vibrations and signal processing for automotive/aerospace/construction. Recommend it only if his priority shifts to 'get to Europe with a real, fundable, visa-safe technical degree and build the music career on the side in Barcelona' — which, given his profile and budget sensitivity, is a genuinely defensible strategy. First action: email admissions to confirm (a) Software Engineering counts as a 'similar' degree, (b) the tuition figure, (c) the IELTS band.

program: Máster de Formación Permanente en Producción Musical (semipresencial)
institution: UCAM — Universidad Católica San Antonio de Murcia
institutionType: Private university (Catholic, private, Murcia).
qualification: TÍTULO PROPIO — specifically a 'Máster de Formación Permanente'. This is UCAM's OWN diploma, 60 ECTS, NOT an official Máster Universitario. It does not appear in the official RUCT catalogue of official degrees and does not give direct access to a Spanish doctorate.
accreditationStatus: NOT OFFICIAL as a degree. It is a título propio / Máster de Formación Permanente issued by UCAM. UCAM itself is a fully recognised Spanish private university (so the institution is legitimate and appears in RUCT), but THIS AWARD is not an ANECA-verified official master. visaEligible: PROBABLY, BUT UNVERIFIED AND RISKY. Spanish student visas require full-time study at an authorised centre; UCAM qualifies as an authorised centre. However this programme is SEMIPRESENCIAL (hybrid), and consulates routinely refuse or downgrade visa applications for programmes that are not full-time face-to-face. He must obtain written confirmation from UCAM's international office that this specific programme supports a type-D student visa before paying anything. Do not assume.
focus: Music production, composition techniques, artistic development, recording, mixing and mastering.
whatYouStudy: Composition and production techniques, artistic development, all phases of creating and recording a musical work, mixing and mastering. Graduates exit as music producer, mixing specialist, mastering technician or studio assistant engineer. Steinberg Cubase professional certification is awarded on completion.
durationEcts: 60 ECTS, one academic year.
language: Spanish. NOTE: he must be able to study in Spanish — this is a hard blocker if his Spanish is not strong.
intakes: One intake per year (academic year start; UCAM postgraduate courses typically begin in October). Exact 2027 start date UNVERIFIED.
tuitionPerYear: EUR 3,900 academic fee per course year (published on the UCAM programme page). Same fee applies to non-EU students — UCAM does not publish a separate international rate.
tuitionTotal: EUR 3,900 total tuition for the whole 60-ECTS programme. Academic year of reference: the currently advertised edition (2026/2027) — confirm for 2027/2028.
otherFees: Pre-enrolment fee EUR 235 (non-refundable). School insurance EUR 59.12. No other fees published.
equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Given the semipresencial format, a capable laptop and a DAW licence should be assumed; Cubase certification is included in the programme.

entryRequirements: An official university degree or equivalent higher-education qualification (Grado or official master level). The page explicitly welcomes graduates in Audiovisual Communication, Journalism, Musicology, Music Education, TELECOMMUNICATIONS OR COMPUTER ENGINEERING, and professional conservatory diploma holders. Only 12 places.

A BSc in Software Engineering maps directly onto this. This is one of the very few programmes in the slice where his degree is named as a welcome background.
portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published — UNVERIFIED. Admission is through the UCAM postgraduate admissions portal.
englishTest: Not applicable — the programme is in Spanish. No IELTS needed. But Spanish-language capability will be required (level not published — UNVERIFIED).
applicationOpens: Rolling through the UCAM admissions portal (www.ucam.edu/admision). Exact 2027 opening UNVERIFIED.
deadline: No published deadline; places are limited to 12 so effectively first-come. UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle.
scholarships: No scholarship specifically identified for non-EU applicants on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. UCAM's general postgraduate financing is described as 'payment plans and financing options available through banking entities', which realistically requires a Spanish bank relationship.
paymentPlans: Yes — payment plans and financing through partner banking entities are advertised, terms UNVERIFIED.
facilities: Campus de los Jerónimos, Murcia. Programme partners: Sony Music España and the MasterFather platform. Teaching by working producers including Ludovico Vagnone, Antonio Escobar, Ed Is Dead, Pablo Rous, Baghira and Luis del Toro. Official Steinberg Cubase certification included.
reputationSignals: Real industry partnership with Sony Music España; genuinely well-known Spanish producers on the teaching staff (Ed Is Dead and Baghira are recognised names in Spanish electronic music); Steinberg certification is a concrete, verifiable credential. UCAM absorbed/rebranded its older 'Máster en Ingeniería de Sonido y Producción Discográfica' into this programme (the old URL now resolves to this one) — so treat any listing of the sound-engineering master as superseded. Red flag: only 12 places and a hybrid format; and the award is a certificate, not a degree.
recommendation: The best VALUE in this slice by an enormous margin: EUR 4,194 all-in for a 60-ECTS university-branded music production master with Sony Music involvement and named Spanish electronic producers teaching. His software-engineering degree is explicitly listed as a welcome entry profile, no portfolio is demanded, and no IELTS is needed. Three serious caveats he must resolve before treating it as a plan: (1) it is a TÍTULO PROPIO, not an official master — legally a certificate; (2) it is SEMIPRESENCIAL, which is the classic reason a Spanish consulate refuses a student visa — get written visa confirmation from UCAM first; (3) it is taught in Spanish. If he can clear the visa and the language, this is the highest return-on-euro option available to him in Spain. If the visa answer is no, it is worthless to him as a relocation route.
